segments.title: The break, and the acceptance test
sections: The Break You Bought At The Top

cues.text: You know this one. Price runs at the prior-day high, a level, a price you marked before the session. It pokes through, the bar is green and getting longer, and you buy it.
Two minutes later price is back inside the prior session’s range, and your stop, a few points under your fill because there was nothing else to put it behind, is gone.
Twenty minutes after that, price goes through the high again and keeps going, without you.
One cause, twice. You traded the movement through the level, not the level’s answer to it.
Now, the chain. Every trade here runs idea, then setup, then trigger, then construction. The setup is a named location plus a read of what price does there, judged on a closed bar.
At a level, price either holds or fails. When the move through it holds, the setup is Trend Continuation. When it fails, it is Range Rejection, Module 11.
Now, the test. Acceptance means price builds time and volume at a new price instead of passing through it.
Here it is mechanical: a 5-minute close beyond the zone, the band around the level, within 15 minutes of the first touch.
The example, on a composite chart with invented prices. A prior-day high zone, 24,312 to 24,318, with price arriving from below. The first touch prints at 9:52.
Fifteen minutes later is 10:07, so the closes that count are 9:55, 10 a.m., and 10:05.
The 10 a.m. bar closes at 24,331.25, above the top of the zone. Accepted above.
A 1-minute spike to 24,326 that closes back at 24,316 is not acceptance. Neither is a close above the zone at 10:15. The window shut at 10:07.
Beyond the zone means beyond the whole band, not beyond the price you think of as the level.
The rule: the read is acceptance only when a 5-minute bar closes beyond the zone within 15 minutes of the first touch. Anything else is no Trend Continuation.
Getting it wrong is saying it broke the high about a bar that is still open, or about a wick. A wick is a rumor. A close is a statement.
The fix: the setup goes in the journal only with a time and a price. Trend-continuation, 5-minute close 24,331.25 at 10 a.m. If you cannot write the close and its time, the field stays empty.

check.q: Which bar counts as acceptance at a zone?
options: A 5-minute close beyond the whole zone, within 15 minutes of the first touch
Any bar that trades through the zone
A 1-minute close beyond the near edge
check.why: The read is a 5-minute close beyond the whole band, inside the 15-minute window. A wick or a 1-minute spike is not acceptance.

check.q: The first touch is at 9:52. Which close can still count?
check.why: Fifteen minutes from 9:52 is 10:07. The 10:05 close is inside it; 10:10 and 10:15 are after the window shut.

check.q: A zone runs 24,312 to 24,318 and price arrives from below. A bar closes at 24,316. What is it?
options: Acceptance, it is above the level you think of
Acceptance, it passed the near edge
A close inside the zone, so no acceptance
check.why: Beyond the zone means beyond the whole band. A close inside the zone is a close inside the zone.

check.q: Saying “it broke the high” about a bar that is still open reveals what?
options: A strong read of the trend
You are reading the bar you want, not the bar that closed
check.why: The read then changes every few seconds with your hopes. The fix is a setup field filled only with a close and its time.

segments.title: The first touch, and the trigger
sections: The First Touch And The Test Number
The Trigger Lives In The Pullback

cues.text: The clock needs a start, and the start is a price you can point at: the first touch, the first trade inside the zone on a test of it.
Write its time, and the deadline next to it. Pd-high, the slug, the short name you log a level under, for the prior-day high. Touch 9:52, deadline 10:07.
Now, the test number: how many times price has come to a zone in the session. The first touch is test 1.
The next touch is test 2, and a test ends when price leaves the zone beyond either edge.
So a pullback into a zone that price was accepted beyond is test 2.
The rule: at the first touch, write the time, the deadline and the test number. Whether a second test behaves like the first, only your record can say, and only if every trade carries the number.
Now, the trigger, the price event at the level that tells you to enter. Acceptance says which way the level answered, not when.
The acceptance bar is the read. It is not the invitation. The entry comes after, when price pulls back to the zone and something happens there.
The trigger here is Pause N Go, from Module 13. The pause: two 1-minute bars in a row hold inside the zone, with no close through its far edge, the side away from where price arrives.
The go: a 1-minute close beyond the pause’s high, in the direction of the read. The entry is on that close.
Show it. After the 10 a.m. acceptance, price runs to 24,352.50 and comes back. At 10:14 it touches 24,318, the zone’s top. That is test 2.
The 10:15 and 10:16 bars trade entirely inside the zone, with a high of 24,318. That is the pause.
The 10:17 bar closes at 24,321, above that high. That is the go.
Order flow can confirm a trigger. It is never the trigger.
The rule: after acceptance, the entry is a named trigger that fires in the pullback, with price at the zone. No pullback to the zone, no trade.
Getting it wrong is a long 30 points above the zone because the move confirmed. That trade has the level’s direction and none of its structure.
The fix: arm the ticket only after two lines are written: the acceptance close with its time, and the trigger with its price.

segments.title: The stop behind the far edge
sections: The Stop Goes Behind The Far Edge

cues.text: The stop goes behind the far edge, the edge of the zone on the far side from where price arrives.
In a continuation trade price meets the zone twice, from opposite sides. On the first touch it comes from below, and the far edge is the top. That is the edge acceptance closes beyond.
On the pullback it comes from above, so the far edge is now the bottom. That is the edge your stop goes behind.
The example. The zone is 24,312 to 24,318. The entry is 24,321. The stop is 24,310, two points behind 24,312, and below both pause lows.
Risk is 11 points, 44 ticks, a tick being a quarter point.
If price trades through the whole zone and fills that stop, the level you were trading has stopped holding. The trade is over by the same fact that started it.
Now, the invalidation: on a branch, one if-then line of your plan, the price, judged on a candle close, at which the thesis is wrong. Here: a 5-minute close back below 24,312.
The stop is the resting order. The invalidation is the close that ends the thesis whether or not the stop has filled.
If your own stop floor, the smallest stop you allow at that time of day, is wider than the far edge, the stop goes out to the floor and the size falls.
A wider stop changes the size, never the risk.
The rule: the stop is a resting order behind the far edge on the far side of acceptance, sent with the entry, and never widened.
Getting it wrong is a stop under the low of the trigger bar, inside the zone, because it made the size bigger. The chart does not know how big you wanted to be.
Ordinary noise inside the zone can then end a trade whose level never broke.
The fix: write the far edge and the stop as a pair before the session. Far edge 24,312, stop 24,310. If the ticket does not match the line, the order is not sent.

segments.title: The target, and the move that leaves
sections: The Target Is The Next Level
The Move That Leaves Without You

cues.text: A target is a level on your list, in the direction of the trade, normally the next one, written before entry.
It is not a number of R, 1R being your entry to your stop. A fixed 2R is a price nobody else is watching.
The example. From the 24,321 entry, the next level up is the prior-week-high zone, 24,388 to 24,396. The target is its near edge.
That is 67 points of room against 11 of risk, about 6 to 1. The 2 to 1 check says if a trade is allowed, not where it ends.
Now, the planned scale: half off at 2R, 22 points, so 24,343. The other half, the runner, is held to 24,388 with the original stop.
The exits, then. One: the target.
Two: the planned scale.
Three: the stop.
Four: the four reasons to flatten by hand, from Module 02. Any other exit is tagged Too Early.
The rule: the target is a level written before entry, and nothing else exits the trade.
Getting it wrong is everything off at 1.5R because it stalled, or the stop dragged up behind each swing. Fear of giving back is running the exit.
The fix: send target and scale with the entry as resting orders, so your hand can only cancel one.
Now, the move that leaves. Sometimes price is accepted and never comes back. It closes above the zone at 10 a.m. and is at the target by 10:30, no pullback.
A read, never a trigger. That is no trade.
A branch you wrote, coming true without you, feels like a loss. The urge is to enter earlier next time.
On the acceptance bar.
On the first touch.
On the poke through.
Each one trades the movement, not the level. That is the break you bought.
You cannot be stopped out of a trade you did not take. It is the safest position in the market. Keep the count: how often your setup offers no trigger.

The fix: keep the ticket unarmed while price is outside the zone, and write one line instead. Pd-high accepted 10 a.m., no pullback, no trade.

check.q: What is the target in a continuation trade?
options: The high of the acceptance bar
A level from your list in the direction of the trade, written before entry
check.why: The target is a level, normally the next one. A fixed number of R is a price nobody else is looking at.

check.q: Entry 24,321, stop 24,310. Where is the planned scale at 2R?
check.why: 2R is 22 points above the 24,321 entry, so 24,343. The runner then aims at the target level.

check.q: Price is accepted above the zone at 10 a.m. and reaches the target by 10:30 without a pullback. What do you have?
options: A reason to widen the target
A read but no trigger: no trade
check.why: There was a read and never a trigger. Acceptance without a pullback to the zone is no trade, marked and noted, never chased.

check.q: Taking everything off at 1.5R because it stalled reveals what?
options: The exit is being run by fear of giving back open profit
check.why: The plan stopped being the plan the moment the trade went your way. The fix is resting target and scale orders sent with the entry.

cues.text: Three composite sessions, invented prices, one test. Only the level and the context change.
One: the prior-day high, long.
Two: the prior-week low, short.
Three: the developing VPOC, where no trade comes.
Case 1: the prior-day high, long. Zone 24,312 to 24,318. Touch at 9:52, test 1, deadline 10:07.
A 5-minute close at 24,331.25, eight minutes after the touch. Accepted above.
The pullback is test 2, a pause of two bars, a go close at 24,321. Stop 24,310, behind the far edge. Target 24,388.
Case 2: the prior-week low, short. It overlaps the overnight low, so the two are written as one zone, 23,846 to 23,854.
Touch at 10:21, test 1, deadline 10:36. A 5-minute close at 23,839.50, nine minutes after the touch. Accepted below.
The pullback is test 2 at 10:41. The go closes at 23,843, below the pause’s low. Stop 23,856, behind the top of the zone. Target 23,796.
Case 3: the developing VPOC, the price with the most volume so far in the session, as it forms. Zone 24,207 to 24,213, first touch at 12:52, deadline 1:07 p.m.
The closes are 24,209.25, 24,208.75 and 24,211.50. All inside. A 1-minute probe to 24,203.50 is real, fast, and not a close.
No acceptance by the deadline, so no setup. No trigger is looked for, no stop is placed.
One line in the journal: developing-vpoc, test 1, not accepted by 1:07, no trade. It is the shortest trade in the course.
Notice what stayed the same. Each branch was written before price got there, invalidation first. Each read was a 5-minute close against a deadline written at the touch.
Each trigger was the same two held bars and one close, and each stop sat behind the far edge. Conviction, the count of checks the branch passed, did not change the size in any of them.
The rule: one test at every level. Only the zone changes.
Getting it wrong is reading three cases as three different setups. You add a rule for the thin one and drop one for the strong one, and the record stops being a record.

cues.text: Take your last ten trades tagged trend-continuation, or your last ten breaks of a level you traded. Score each one a point for each line that is true.
One, read: a 5-minute bar closed beyond the whole zone within 15 minutes, and you can name the bar.
Two, touch: the first-touch time and the test number were written before the order.
Three, trigger: the entry came on a named trigger in the pullback, with price at the zone.
Four, stop: a resting stop sat behind the far edge, sent with the entry, never widened.
Five, target: a level written before entry, and the only exits were the target, the scale, the stop and the four reasons.
Reading it. Lines one and three override the score. A trade that misses line one had no setup. A trade that misses line three had no trigger at the level.
If two or more of your ten miss line one or three, fix those first: no setup field without a close and its time, and no armed ticket while price is outside the zone.
If none do, find the line from two, four and five that the most trades missed. If three or more missed it, it goes on your pre-market sheet, your written plan, as a check.
Getting it wrong is averaging the score. An average is a comfortable number. The journal does not deal in comfortable numbers.
And a trade that misses line one had no setup, whatever the other four say.
The assignment. Next session, the first time a near-edge alert sounds, the alert set on the side of a zone that price arrives at, write one line before anything else.
The slug, the test number, the touch time and the deadline. Pd-high, test 1, touch 9:52, deadline 10:07.
That is the whole assignment.
In one line: the level asks the question, a 5-minute close inside 15 minutes answers it, and the trade comes only on the pullback.
Without the close there is no setup. Without the pullback there is no trade.
Where it goes next. Module 11, Range Rejection, is the same test with the other answer. Module 12 covers the gap setups, and Module 13 teaches the triggers in full.
Module 14 turns a triggered branch into a stop, the 2 to 1 check and a size. Module 15 writes the plan, and Module 18 is the journal, where every continuation trade carries its test number.

check.q: Which two lines override the score when you review a trade?
check.why: A trade that misses line 1 had no setup; one that misses line 3 had no trigger at the level.

check.q: Two of your ten trades miss line 1 or line 3. What comes first?
options: Nothing: two of ten is normal
Fix those before your next continuation trade
check.why: Two or more misses on line 1 or 3 are fixed first: no setup field without a close and its time, and no armed ticket while price is outside the zone.

check.q: What is the one-line assignment?
options: The slug, test number, touch time and deadline at the first near-edge alert
Mark one trade as an A+
check.why: Write one line the first time a near-edge alert sounds at one of your zones, before anything else.

check.q: Scoring your ten trades from memory reveals what?
options: The journal is a diary rather than a record
check.why: Memory scores generously. Only what is written counts, and a trade that misses line 1 had no setup whatever the other lines say.

questions.q: A 5-minute close beyond the zone counts as acceptance only when it comes…
options: Within 15 minutes of the first touch
On the next bar after a wick
questions.why: The close has to come within 15 minutes of the first touch. After that the window has shut.

options: A 5-minute close beyond the whole zone inside the window
A 1-minute spike that closes back inside
A close beyond the zone at 10:05 after a 9:52 touch
questions.why: A spike that closes back inside is a wick, not a close beyond the zone.

questions.q: You were accepted above a zone, then price returns to it. That touch is…
questions.why: A test ends when price leaves the zone beyond either edge, so the next touch is test 2.
The close is the read. The entry is a named trigger that fires in the pullback, with price at the zone.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on the pullback after acceptance above?
options: Behind the bottom edge, the far edge of acceptance
Inside the zone at the trigger low
questions.why: On the pullback price arrives from above, so the far edge is the bottom; the stop sits behind it.

options: The next level on your list, written before entry
The high of the acceptance bar
questions.why: A target is a level from your list in the direction of the trade, normally the next one.

questions.q: Price is accepted and leaves without a pullback to the zone. You…
options: Enter on the acceptance bar next time
Take no trade and write one line
questions.why: Acceptance without a pullback is no trade. Keep the ticket unarmed and note the line.

questions.q: A 1-minute probe taps below the zone and closes back inside. At the deadline no 5-minute bar has closed beyond it. The setup is…
options: Not there: no trigger is looked for
questions.why: With no read there is no setup, so no trigger is looked for and no stop is placed.
